DIY Biogas Digester User Your Kitchen Waste To Power Your Cooking Devices

All you need to digest organics and harvest gas is an airtight container with some input/output ports. Storing/cleaning the gas will be an issue. You'll need something safe to store in. Humidity in the gas will be an issue, especially if you want to compress it or store it for a while, and contaminants in the gas could be harmful to your health or combustion equipment depending on your organic feedstock.

Here is a good example of what NOT to do: have a high moisture/high sulfide organic mix and try to harvest the gas while storing in a plastic bag (the site says you can store it in a bag. ) You'll Have a liquid waste with the gas from condensation which will be hazardous, and hydrogen sulfide gas contamination (which kills fast). Also, if your feedstock has silica present you'll get buildup on your equipment which will cause damage. A real-world example of this is food waste+drywall decaying in landfills. Many landfills harvest and burn their gas, creating electricity if able, but it is done with many safety checks.

There are more potential issues, these are just a few. If you're really interested in digesting, be safe. Build outside in a well -ventilated area. Think about how you'll clean, store, and use your gas. Pay attention to your feedstock- what goes in comes out.

Source: I design and oversee construction of gas collection and transmission systems for landfills. BSE in Environmental Engineering. Been out of school for almost two years and (slowly) working on my engineering license.

Edit: I forgot to mention that digestion reaction temperatures can routinely get up to around the 145F mark, so be careful. If you have a larger digester with lots of gas an explosion can occur if oxygen is introduced.
